reason: The text explicitly documents the Israelite community's antagonism toward their leaders Moses and Aaron. Multiple passages show direct complaints against them: 'וַיִּלֹּנוּ עַל־ מֹשֶׁה וְעַֽל־ אַהֲרֹן כֹּל בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל' (they complained against Moses and against Aaron, all the Israelites). The people express wishes to die and question why Moses brought them to the land. Furthermore, the community threatens violence against the scouts who support the leadership: 'וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ כָּל־ הָעֵדָה לִרְגּוֹם אֹתָם בָּאֲבָנִים' (the whole community said to stone them). God Himself later describes the people as spurning Him and complaining against Him, referencing the people's antagonism toward the leadership journey. Joshua and Caleb are notably set apart as supporters of the leaders, while the broader community displays clear hostility and defiance.
